svg.title: Jobs within 60 minutes by public transport, by income decile, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Belo Horizonte
svg.desc: Three panels of box plots, one per city, of the share of the city's formal jobs reached within 60 minutes by public transport from the cells of each income decile. In all three cities access rises with income. The richest tenth reaches on average 7.9 times as many jobs as the poorest four tenths in São Paulo, 2.3 times as many jobs as the poorest four tenths in Rio de Janeiro, 2.0 times as many jobs as the poorest four tenths in Belo Horizonte.

g.text: Income decile (per capita income of the cell)
Share of the city's formal jobs reached from each cell, by income decile of its residents (Censo 2010),
weighted by population. Boxes: quartiles and median; lines: 10th to 90th percentile. Palma ratio: the mean
of the richest tenth over the mean of the poorest four tenths. Morning peak, Tuesday 17 November 2026
Jobs within an hour by public transport, by income
Streets © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), Geofabrik extract of 2026-11-01. GTFS: SPTrans (São Paulo), SMTR (Rio de Janeiro, CC BY 4.0),
SUMOB (Belo Horizonte, CC BY). Cells, population and income (Censo 2010), jobs (RAIS 2019), schools and health facilities (2019): Ipea, aopdata.
